path_decisions.rationale: Pheromone strong (0.097). The signal pipeline must be fixed before risk filtering can be effective — good signals getting canceled before reaching risk engine
Position sizer's hardcoded win_rate=0.5 causes systematic mis-sizing. Each strategy should contribute its actual performance to the Kelly formula
MACD is used in trend_following (fast=12, slow=26, signal=9) — standard equity settings. For crypto with faster cycles, shorter MACD periods may capture more trend starts

None of the MACD/RSI/ATR parameters are in any param_space for optimization. The entire param tuning infrastructure exists (optimizer.py) but the search spaces are not defined for per-strategy optimization

candidate_solution.summary: 4 changes: (1) fix consolidation, (2) strategy-specific Kelly, (3) crypto MACD params, (4) define full param_spaces for optimization

change_1.title: Add MACD parameters to optimization param_space with crypto-appropriate ranges
change_1.current: macd_fast=12, macd_slow=26, macd_signal=9 — standard equity settings from 1970s. Crypto markets operate on shorter timeframes with faster trend development.
change_1.proposed: Add macd_fast (range [6, 18]), macd_slow (range [18, 40]), macd_signal (range [5, 15]) to param_space. Default search centers around current values but allows the optimizer to explore faster MACD settings. For 4H crypto charts, MACD 8/21/7 often outperforms 12/26/9. For daily charts, 12/26/9 may still be optimal. The optimizer should find the right value per timeframe.
change_1.rationale: MACD parameters control when the trend signal fires. Standard 12/26/9 was designed for weekly equity charts. Crypto 4H charts have ~4x more bars per week. Faster MACD detects trend changes earlier, entering before the move is extended. Earlier entries in trends have higher win_rate because they capture more of the directional move.

change_2.title: Define complete per-strategy param_spaces with all tunable parameters
change_2.current: The optimize command exists but the param_space dict passed to StrategyOptimizer.optimize() only contains a few parameters per strategy. Most strategy parameters (MACD periods, RSI periods, BB std, ATR multiplier, volume threshold) are NOT in any param_space.
change_2.proposed: For each strategy template, define a complete param_space dict in a new file quantflow/config/strategies/{name}_param_space.json containing ALL tunable parameters. For trend_following: fast_ma_period, slow_ma_period, macd_fast, macd_slow, macd_signal, rsi_period, rsi_overbought, rsi_oversold, atr_period, atr_multiplier, volume_period, volume_threshold, min_conditions, profit_take_pct, trailing_stop_atr_mult, max_holding_bars. The CLI optimize command loads this file and passes it to the optimizer.
change_2.rationale: The optimizer can only find optimal parameters for what's in the param_space. Currently most parameters are hardcoded and excluded from optimization. Adding them all to param_space enables the optimizer to find the globally optimal parameter set for win_rate. This is the infrastructure change that makes all the other parameter-tuning proposals testable.

change_3.title: Populate PositionSizer with per-strategy actual win_rate from backtest results
change_3.current: TradingSession creates PositionSizer with default win_rate=0.5. The BacktestResult from each strategy run contains actual win_rate but it's not fed back to PositionSizer.
change_3.proposed: After running backtests for each strategy, store BacktestResult.win_rate in a strategy_win_rates dict. Pass this dict to PositionSizer via new constructor param or setter method. When sizing a signal, PositionSizer looks up signal.strategy_id in strategy_win_rates. This makes Kelly sizing strategy-aware.
change_3.rationale: Kelly criterion: f* = (p*b - q)/b where p = win_rate. Using wrong p produces wrong position size. If actual win_rate is 0.55 but we use 0.5, we under-bet by ~15%, leaving profit on the table. If actual is 0.42, we over-bet by ~30%, increasing loss severity. Correct Kelly sizing maximizes geometric growth rate which indirectly maximizes win_rate by ensuring we stay in the game long enough for the edge to manifest.

change_4.title: Track per-strategy risk events and auto-adjust risk budgets
change_4.current: RiskEngine records events to Prometheus (RISK_EVENTS counter) but doesn't use the history to adjust behavior. All strategies get the same limits forever.
change_4.proposed: Add strategy_risk_state dict to RiskEngine tracking per-strategy: consecutive_losses, daily_pnl, weekly_pnl. After N consecutive losses (configurable, default=5), temporarily reduce that strategy's position_limit_pct by 50% (de-risk). After a win, restore to full. This is a self-adjusting circuit breaker per strategy.
change_4.rationale: Strategies in drawdown tend to have lower short-term win_rate. Reducing position size during drawdowns limits losses while maintaining exposure. When the strategy recovers, full sizing resumes. This adaptive approach maintains higher portfolio-level win_rate by reducing exposure to cold strategies and maximizing exposure to hot ones.

notes: The param_space gap is the meta-finding: the optimizer exists but most parameters aren't searchable. Adding complete param_spaces is the prerequisite infrastructure that makes all parameter-tuning proposals testable. Without it, every parameter change is manual trial-and-error. With it, Optuna can systematically find optimal parameter combinations across all dimensions simultaneously.
